title: Scale, flip and offset
learned: GAIN scales a voltage: below 1 smaller, above 1 bigger, at 0 nothing
Left of 0 the voltage is flipped upside down
OFFSET adds a fixed voltage; with nothing patched a row is a voltage knob
A square wave on pitch jumps between two notes: a trill

steps.why: Outputs rarely give exactly the voltage an input needs: too much, too little, or the wrong way up. An attenuverter fixes that: it attenuates (makes smaller), inverts (flips) and offsets (shifts) a voltage. It works on any voltage, audio or CV.
steps.do: A drone with vibrato plays: SIN of the LFO goes to FM of the oscillator. The attenuverter (JX-ATT) has four rows, each with GAIN and OFFSET. Press Next.

steps.why: Put the attenuverter between the LFO and the oscillator.
steps.do: Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from SIN of the LFO to IN 1 of the attenuverter (SIN already has a cable). Then drag a cable from OUT 1 of the attenuverter to FM of the oscillator: it replaces the direct cable there.
steps.after: The vibrato sounds the same: GAIN of row 1 starts at 1×, which passes the voltage unchanged.

steps.do: Press F1 and turn GAIN of row 1 slowly from the right, through the middle, to the left.
steps.after: Toward the middle the vibrato gets smaller and stops at 0. Left of the middle it comes back upside down: the pitch now goes down where it went up. You rarely hear the flip on a vibrato, but on an envelope it turns 'opens on each note' into 'closes on each note'.

steps.why: OFFSET adds a fixed voltage to whatever comes through.
steps.do: Turn OFFSET of row 1 a bit away from 0.
steps.after: The whole pitch moved: the vibrato now swings around a different note. With nothing patched into a row, it gives a steady voltage you set with GAIN and OFFSET: a knob you can patch anywhere.
steps.try: Double-click OFFSET to put it back to 0.

steps.why: A square wave has only two values. On pitch, that means two notes.
steps.do: Press F2 and drag a cable from SQR of the LFO to IN 1 of the attenuverter (it replaces the SIN cable).
steps.after: The pitch now jumps between two notes: a trill. GAIN sets how far apart they are, RATE of the LFO how fast it jumps.
steps.try: Press F1 and turn GAIN of row 1 until the two notes sound good together.

steps.do: Scale, flip, shift: with an attenuverter any voltage fits any input. Press Next to finish.
